title: Hawkish ECB Minutes Reinforce Expectations of a December Rate Hike
intro: The minutes of the European Central Bank's October policy meeting have delivered a markedly hawkish signal to markets, confirming that the Governing Council is tilting firmly toward further monetary tightening. While the deposit rate was held unanimously at 2.50%, the internal deliberations revealed that a sizeable group of policymakers was already prepared to support an immediate hike — a posture that, combined with accelerating inflation data at both the consumer and producer levels, has pushed overnight index swap markets to price in a 94.4% implied probability of a 25-basis-point increase at the December 17 meeting.

sections.heading: A Unanimous Hold With a Clear Hawkish Undercurrent
sections.content: The ECB's decision to maintain the deposit rate at 2.50% in October was reached by consensus, yet the unanimity of the hold obscures a meaningful internal division over timing rather than direction. A sizeable contingent of Governing Council members argued that the deterioration in the inflation outlook had already justified a move at the October meeting itself, with the remaining debate centred solely on when — not whether — to act. Critically, all Governing Council members assessed inflation risks as tilted to the upside. The minutes also flagged a heightened concern over second-round effects: if wage growth accelerates as workers seek compensation for eroded purchasing power and firms subsequently pass those costs through to end consumers, inflation could remain durably above the ECB's 2% target even into 2028. Adding to the hawkish tone, some members noted that the current 2.50% deposit rate still falls within the estimated range for the neutral rate, implying that monetary policy is providing only limited restraint at present — a signal that the bar for additional tightening remains relatively low.

sections.heading: Inflation Dynamics: Consumer and Producer Pressures Both Intensify
sections.content: The inflation data released alongside the October meeting minutes reinforced the ECB's cautious stance. Eurozone headline HICP inflation rose to 4.0% year on year in October, up from 3.8% in September, matching consensus expectations. On a monthly basis, prices increased 0.5%, above the 0.4% forecast and following a 0.6% gain in September. Core inflation — which strips out volatile energy and food components and is closely monitored by the Governing Council as a gauge of underlying price persistence — climbed to 2.6% year on year from 2.5%, exceeding the 2.5% market forecast. The monthly core reading accelerated to 0.3% from 0.2%, in line with expectations. Price pressures were equally pronounced at the producer level. Eurozone producer price inflation surged to 11.1% year on year in September, sharply above the prior reading of 8.3% and ahead of the 10.9% consensus estimate. The monthly increase registered at 2.5%, consistent with forecasts and up from 2.0% previously. The extent to which these upstream cost pressures translate into further consumer price inflation will depend on corporate pricing power and demand conditions — but the concurrent rise in core CPI gives the ECB clear empirical grounds to monitor whether inflationary momentum is becoming entrenched.

sections.heading: Swap Markets Fully Price December, Signal Gradual Tightening Through 2027
sections.content: Bloomberg's WIRP snapshot as of November 27 showed overnight index swaps implying 23.6 basis points of additional tightening by the December 17 meeting, translating to a 94.4% implied probability of a standard 25-basis-point hike. Such a move would bring the ECB's deposit rate to 2.75%. The implied overnight rate of 2.681% embedded in the WIRP screen reflects this expectation, measured against a current effective overnight rate of 2.445%. Beyond December, the swap curve points to a gradual and measured tightening cycle extending into 2027. Markets are pricing approximately 42 basis points of cumulative tightening by March 2027, rising to 53 basis points by June and approximately 59 basis points by October — equivalent to roughly 2.3 standard quarter-point hikes from current levels in total, inclusive of the December move. This trajectory is consistent with the Governing Council's stated preference for gradualism, preserving optionality for reassessment at each successive meeting.

quote: Overnight index swaps priced a 94.4% implied probability of a 25bp ECB hike on December 17, with approximately 59 basis points of cumulative tightening priced through October 2027 — Bloomberg WIRP, November 27.
conclusion: The December ECB meeting assumes pivotal significance well beyond the rate decision itself. With a 25-basis-point hike already near-fully discounted by markets, the more consequential market catalyst will likely be the forward guidance embedded in the ECB's updated staff macroeconomic projections — which will, for the first time, extend the forecast horizon to 2029. Should those projections reveal inflation remaining above target for a prolonged period, or if wage settlement data indicate persistent cost-push dynamics, traders may move to price a faster pace of tightening into the 2027 curve. Conversely, a materially more favourable inflation trajectory could soften expectations for the post-December path, even if the near-term hike proceeds as anticipated. The minutes have made the ECB's directional bias unambiguous. What remains open is the cadence — and December's projections will be the primary instrument through which the Governing Council communicates its answer.
excerpt: Hawkish ECB minutes and rising inflation data push markets to near-fully price a December rate hike to 2.75%.
